title: D1b Ownership And Internal Scoped Operations
summary: Dev68/schema033 adds personal checkpoint, preparation, active-route mutation and cleanup HTTP over existing native services. Explicit ownership, RLS, CAS, retries and artifact pins remain. Named publications stay deferred; device login, client wiring and a bounded pilot remain.
releasePolicy: Personal workspaces are isolated by tenant and owner. Cross-user sharing and shared knowledge-base publication are outside the current delivery scope; existing history and pins remain protected.

binding.authority: Only the explicitly trusted configured maintenance administrator can bind existing registry projects/workspaces. Tenant roles, static project grants and caller headers cannot bind or transfer ownership.
binding.project: Exactly one tenant per existing project. Unassigned rows are not inferred from paths, names, prior grants or source hosts.
binding.workspace: The enabled personal-space owner must own every new bound workspace. Visibility defaults to private; shared requests and cross-owner bindings return403 sharing-disabled. Historical flags/bindings remain stored, but no cross-user access follows. Composite foreign keys remain enforced.
binding.retry: An exact binding retry returns replayed=true without another audit event. Different tenant, owner or visibility returns409 identity-conflict; no transfer, deletion or visibility-edit API in this slice.
binding.transaction: Binding and metadata-only audit commit together under the existing directory mutation advisory lock. Audit failure rolls back the binding. Existing DB deadlines, request and pool bounds remain.

routes.access: Actual active personal-space owner or explicit maintenance; metadata only
Actual active personal-space owner or explicit maintenance
Actual active owner; inconsistent historical cross-owner bindings are hidden. Explicit maintenance remains privileged. Metadata only
Actual personal-space and workspace owner, or explicit maintenance

authorization.metadata: Resolve enabled account, actual tenant owner, enabled owner membership and workspace owner in each transaction. A foreign membership, even labelled owner, grants nothing. Absent and foreign resources return the same404 identity-not-found.
authorization.output: Only tenant_id/project_id and workspace_id/owner_id/visibility as appropriate, plus content_access=scoped-routes-only. Inventory items also include display_name; detail responses remain unchanged. No root paths, source, vectors or historical payloads.
authorization.rls: Three new ENABLE/FORCE RLS tables, runtime non-owner/non-BYPASSRLS. Six authorization GUCs are transaction-local and reset per scope. Trusted legacy project grants are supplied only by Server configuration to admission checks, never by request headers.
authorization.drift: Readiness and transactions check columns, RLS/owner flags, exact six policies, keys/checks/composite FKs and private default. Constraint/policy drift fails closed. PostgreSQL deparser changes need separate qualification.
authorization.boundary: RLS prevents application scoping mistakes, not a malicious holder of the runtime DB password, same-UID attacker, database owner or superuser. Maintenance remains explicitly privileged and is not a normal tenant role.

dataFence.enrolled: All enrolled users remain denied on legacy data routes with403 identity-data-plane-not-enabled.
dataFence.legacy: If any configured grant of an unenrolled non-admin principal intersects a bound project, its non-directory HTTP requests are denied with403 identity-data-plane-not-enabled. This intentionally fences the whole principal, including unrelated granted projects, legacy paths only; personal paths require live workspace admission. Unrelated unenrolled principals retain their existing grants.
dataFence.health: Process liveness remains public; authenticated readiness remains available unless the account is disabled. Binding endpoints and metadata reads remain under identity routes.
dataFence.revocation: Scoped reads and private checkpoint mutations use the rechecks described below. Other admitted/queued work is not yet qualified against revocation. No claim that all jobs, receipts, cache entries, source data or vectors are tenant-isolated.
dataFence.operations: Only use explicit migrations/bindings on a reviewed isolated stand with prior writers stopped. Do not expose this development listener publicly or use this slice for shared onboarding.

migration.preservation: Migrations001..032 remain byte-identical. Observer stream/tombstone tenant coordinates begin NULL; no inferred historical ownership. Old payloads, hashes, sequence progress, quota counters and receipts remain exact. No consumer installation.
migration.rollback: Restore a matched previous binary/configuration/data set in a separate reviewed contour. Old binaries reject schema033; no live down-migration or mixed-version operation.
